subject.title: All .large bubbles should have scrollable body regardless of truncation

question: Should native chat keep transcript-level reader-managed scrolling as the sole long-content interaction, or add an independently scrollable bounded body for a deliberately defined large-bubble class?
rationale: Current behavior deliberately addresses reading position at the transcript level, while this request introduces nested scrolling and needs an intentional cross-platform UX and accessibility contract before a code change can be judged correct.

options.title: Retain transcript-level reading
options.body: Treat the merged reader-managed transcript model as the canonical long-content interaction and close this request unless a concrete native usability failure is reproduced.

options.title: Add a bounded bubble reader
options.body: Define the precise large-content rule and add matching iOS and Android inner-body scrolling with gesture, streaming, and accessibility proof.

options.title: Prototype before committing
options.body: Request a small native design comparison on both platforms before selecting one permanent interaction model.

recommendation.title: Retain transcript-level reading
recommendation.body: Treat the merged reader-managed transcript model as the canonical long-content interaction and close this request unless a concrete native usability failure is reproduced.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged native reader-scroll implementation is the closest current behavior whose interaction contract would be extended or displaced.
